title: Three Seasons and One Short Whistle
subtitle: 体育与运动 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）
meta: 主题语境：体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）　|　核心词汇：training　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 training 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1970 the coach ① gave the training that no player in the field would have counted, and he said the giving was the whole of the season. The ② training, meaning the practice itself and not the whistle, ran three seasons and stayed uncounted in the book; training, he said, is the only thing in a field that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ sort of training in that field had the same short whistle beside it, and the ④ training at the far stand, meaning the goal they kept for the children to cheer and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Training, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the coach said the counting is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the training was the whole of the matter, meaning the discipline and not the practice. The ⑥ training, meaning the discipline and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; training, he said, is either something you give or the only word that means both practice and a discipline. He said the discipline is the part they remember.

By 1975 the ⑦ training had become a line in a record, and the record had become an argument about the short whistle. The ⑧ training of the whole thing, the coach wrote in April, was one field and three seasons of counting; training, he said, is either the goal at the far stand or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ training I remember is the training counted in the record, which closed in 1977 and is still counted as the quietest in the field. ⑩ Training, my mother said in 1979, is the only thing that improves by being counted; all training, she said, is a discipline that has agreed to look like practice. She said the discipline was the honest half.
